label: fig:corpus-blocking
caption: Provider block rate for Gemini against the stated age, per cent of requests submitted, with pointwise 95 per cent bootstrap intervals over scenarios. Panel (a) is every harm domain and rests on 200 scenarios a condition; panel (b) is the domain carrying most of the blocking and rests on 20, which is why its intervals are much wider. No pairwise age-to-age contrast was tested, so the individual points are descriptive; the inferential evidence is the two planned contrasts reported in the supplement. Open markers at eighteen and twenty-one are conditions in which no scenario blocked: every bootstrap resample is then a vector of noughts and the interval has no width, which is the nonparametric bootstrap failing at the boundary rather than a precise estimate of zero, so no bar is drawn. The dotted line marks the benchmark boundary at eighteen, shown for reference only: it is the age at which the design changes the expected action on Age Restricted scenarios, and nothing here assumes it is a blocking threshold. The control condition and all four implicit cues are omitted: they do not sit on an age axis, and all five are at or below 0.17 per cent.

label: fig:safety-trajectory
caption: Refusal Rate against the stated age on Age Restricted scenarios, per cent of returned responses, one line a model. Rates are scenario weighted: replicates are averaged within a scenario and condition before conditions are averaged. The dashed line is the benchmark adult boundary at eighteen, the age at which the design changes the expected answer on these scenarios. The equivalent figure for the three control strata, where the expected answer does not change with age, is in the supplement.

label: fig:safety-primary
caption: The three primary contrasts on Refusal Rate within Age Restricted scenarios, percentage points with 95 per cent bootstrap intervals over scenarios, paired within scenario. A positive effect means more refusal at the younger or the more explicit condition. The three panels share a horizontal scale, so a wider interval cannot read as a larger effect. The macro-average weights the six models equally, is descriptive of this panel, and carries no test.

label: fig:safety-trajectory-all
caption: Refusal Rate against the stated age in all four scenario types, per cent of returned responses. Panels (a), (b) and (d) are the planned controls, where the expected answer is the same at every age; panel (c) is the stratum the primary hypotheses are tested in and carries the benchmark adult boundary.

label: tab:corpus-flow
caption: Corpus flow by model. Submitted is the full design, 200 scenarios under 13 conditions with three replicates. A provider-blocked request returned no response text, so Returned is the denominator of every response-conditional safety rate. It is not the denominator of the block rate, which counts requests that never returned, nor of the end-to-end sensitivity analysis. All 46,640 returned responses were assigned to one of the four outcome cells; the two counts are identical by construction and the identity is asserted rather than shown as a third column. Readability missingness is specific to the measure rather than to the reply, so no single readability denominator is added here.

label: tab:corpus-blocking
caption: Provider block rate for Gemini, per cent of requests submitted, by condition and harm domain. Only domains with at least one Gemini provider block are shown. Blocking is overwhelmingly concentrated in the conditions that state a minor age explicitly: the observed rate is broadly flat across the child and adolescent ages, is lower at age seventeen, and no block was observed at eighteen, at twenty-one, or under the control condition. It is not zero everywhere outside those conditions, since one implicit condition blocked two requests. Denominators differ sharply between columns: the All Domains rate rests on 200 scenarios a condition and the Sexual Content rate on 20, which is why the figure carries intervals and this grid does not. Rates are over submitted requests, the only denominator on which a blocked request can be counted.

label: tab:corpus-unanimity
caption: Replicate unanimity, per cent of scenario x condition cells in which all three replicates gave the same result, with 95 per cent bootstrap intervals over scenarios. Computed only on cells where all three replicates returned a response, since a provider-blocked request carries no outcome cell and a wholly blocked cell would otherwise count as unanimous on a value it does not have. The final column is the gap between the two, and is where the variability sits: a wide gap means the answer held while the delivery did not. This characterises stochastic variability at the fixed sampling setting and does not bound the size of any effect reported later.

label: tab:corpus-reliability
caption: Agreement between the human annotator and the classifier on the two characteristics that constitute the primary outcome, on a calibration sample of six hundred responses drawn one hundred a model. The prevalence columns give the share each annotator marked positive, where positive is Refusal for Answer and Yes for Delivery Response. The classifier was run again on those six hundred replies under the same policy rather than scored on the labels it produced in the main pass, so the coefficient carries the classifier own run- to-run variation as well as its disagreement with the annotator, and is the more conservative of the two comparisons available. Intervals are percentile intervals from four thousand resamples of the annotated rows. Because the sample was also used to refine the rubric, these are calibration figures and not an independent validation.

label: tab:corpus-denominators
caption: The denominator of every safety rate reported in the thesis. Eligible submitted counts the requests the design allocates to that subset. The analysis denominator is what each rate is computed over, which for every rate but the first is the subset of those requests that returned a response. Available is the ratio, and is the only column that reflects data loss rather than design allocation. The block rate is the exception: its denominator is the submitted request rather than the returned response, since a request that never came back is exactly what it counts, so it is available in full by construction.

label: tab:corpus-blocking-tests
caption: Provider blocking contrasts, paired within scenario, percentage points with 95 per cent bootstrap intervals over scenarios and Benjamini and Hochberg values adjusted within the platform blocking family of twelve tests. Every model is tested, including those that blocked nothing and so return an effect of exactly zero: admitting only the models that blocked would select on the outcome being tested. Both contrasts establish an association between a provider- blocked request and an explicitly stated minor age; neither identifies the mechanism that produced it. The family is secondary and is not merged into the primary family.

label: tab:corpus-unanimity-excluded
caption: Cells excluded from the unanimity table, and whether the blocking that excluded them was itself consistent. Provider-status unanimity is the share of cells whose three replicates all went the same way, all returned or all blocked, and is defined on every cell rather than only on complete ones. The final column is the leave-one-model- out sensitivity on the macro-average four-cell unanimity: it is a check on whether that panel figure rests on one member and never replaces it.

label: tab:corpus-reliability-full
caption: Classifier calibration on every annotated characteristic. Rows is the number of pairs the coefficient rests on, which is the full sample except where the judge returned no value. The Use column applies the agreement floor of Cohen kappa 0.70: three characteristics fall below it and are descriptive only, one has no coefficient at all rather than a low one because no positive case appeared in the sample, and one clears the floor at 0.702 on a wide interval and is marked borderline, with a sensitivity withholding it reported in Chapter 5.2. Alternative Response is reported without an interval: the judge returned no value for it on most of the sample in the calibration run, and the saved row-level pairs record those as absent rather than as missing, so the rows behind its coefficient cannot be identified.

label: tab:corpus-unanimity-excluded
caption: Cells excluded from the unanimity table, and whether the blocking that excluded them was itself consistent. Provider-status unanimity is the share of cells whose three replicates all went the same way, all returned or all blocked, and is defined on every cell rather than only on complete ones. The final column is the leave-one-model- out sensitivity on the macro-average four-cell unanimity: it is a check on whether that panel figure rests on one member and never replaces it.

label: tab:corpus-reliability-full
caption: Classifier calibration on every annotated characteristic. Rows is the number of pairs the coefficient rests on, which is the full sample except where the judge returned no value. The Use column applies the agreement floor of Cohen kappa 0.70: three characteristics fall below it and are descriptive only, one has no coefficient at all rather than a low one because no positive case appeared in the sample, and one clears the floor at 0.702 on a wide interval and is marked borderline, with a sensitivity withholding it reported in Chapter 5.2. Alternative Response is reported without an interval: the judge returned no value for it on most of the sample in the calibration run, and the saved row-level pairs record those as absent rather than as missing, so the rows behind its coefficient cannot be identified.

label: tab:corpus-repeatability
caption: Calibration against repeatability. The first two columns are agreement between the human annotator and each of two independent classifier runs, and are calibration. The third is agreement between those two runs, and is repeatability of the judging procedure itself with the human annotation held out of it. The third column is why verdicts in the full corpus pass are not identical to the calibration run on the same replies. That divergence is stochasticity in the procedure and is not a reason to recompute the calibration against a later run of the procedure being calibrated.

label: tab:corpus-repeatability
caption: Calibration against repeatability. The first two columns are agreement between the human annotator and each of two independent classifier runs, and are calibration. The third is agreement between those two runs, and is repeatability of the judging procedure itself with the human annotation held out of it. The third column is why verdicts in the full corpus pass are not identical to the calibration run on the same replies. That divergence is stochasticity in the procedure and is not a reason to recompute the calibration against a later run of the procedure being calibrated.

label: tab:safety-primary
caption: The three primary contrasts, on Refusal Rate within Age Restricted scenarios. Effects are percentage points with 95 per cent bootstrap intervals over scenarios; p is the paired sign-flip permutation value and q is Benjamini and Hochberg adjusted within the primary family of eighteen tests, which is the value each claim rests on. A positive effect means more refusal at the younger or the more explicit condition. The macro-average weights the six models equally, is descriptive of this panel, registered only for its interval, and carries no test, so the eighteen corrected tests are the six models times the three contrasts. One model loses five of twenty-five scenarios to provider-blocked requests, which the supplement reports.

label: tab:safety-alignment
caption: Benchmark Action Alignment, per cent of returned responses whose action matched what the design expects for that scenario at that age. Where a refusal is expected only a Strong Refusal aligns, and where a compliance is expected only a Total Compliance does, so a response that declines and then supplies the content is counted as misaligned. The macro-average weights the six models equally and its interval resamples scenarios under that same weighting. Alignment is agreement with a researcher-defined expectation, not accuracy against an external ground truth. The control condition carries no expected answer on Age Restricted scenarios and is excluded from those two rows.

label: tab:safety-outcome
caption: The primary outcome across all returned responses, per cent. The four cells sum to one hundred. Refusal Rate is Strong plus Weak Refusal and is the measure every contrast in this chapter is run on. Content Delivery Rate is Weak Refusal plus Total Compliance. The final column is the decision-delivery mismatch, the share of responses in the two cells where the stated decision and the delivered content disagree. The macro-average weights the six models equally.

label: tab:safety-outcome-stratum
caption: The outcome within each scenario type, per cent of returned responses. A refusal is the expected answer on Harmful scenarios and the failure mode on Rights and Benign ones, so a corpus-wide refusal rate is not interpretable on its own and this table is the base for every rate reported later.

label: tab:safety-alignment-components
caption: Decision Alignment against Benchmark Action Alignment, per cent of returned responses. Decision Alignment asks only whether the stated decision matched the expected answer and so counts a Weak Refusal on a Harmful scenario as aligned although the content was delivered, and a Minimal Compliance on a Benign one as aligned although nothing was supplied. The gap between the two measures is the decision-delivery mismatch counted against the benchmark. The chapter reports Action Alignment; this table shows what that choice costs and where.

label: tab:safety-deviation
caption: Deviation rates on the primary denominator, per cent of returned responses in the stated subset. Panel A counts content that reached the user where the design expects a refusal. Panel B counts refusals where the design expects the request to be answered.

label: tab:safety-deviation-e2e
caption: The same deviation rates on the end-to-end denominator, per cent of submitted requests, with a provider-blocked request counted as content that did not reach the user and as a request the user could not have answered. A block therefore lowers a delivery rate and raises an over-restriction rate. Each subset is built from the full corpus by scenario type and condition, so a request withheld on every replicate is still counted. This is a secondary sensitivity analysis; the response-conditional view is primary. Only the model that blocked differs between the two.

label: tab:safety-signal-levels
caption: Refusal Rate on Age Restricted scenarios by condition group, per cent of returned responses. The levels behind the signal contrast, so that the effect can be read against where each model sits rather than in isolation. An implicit cue to a minor sits between the adult conditions and a stated minor age on every model.

label: tab:safety-retention
caption: Scenarios entering the trajectory contrast, against what blocking did to the scenario x condition cells behind it. A paired contrast needs a value on both sides of every scenario it uses, and replicates are averaged within a scenario and condition first, so a cell with one reply out of three still contributes. Only a cell with no returned replicate removes its scenario from a contrast that requires that condition. The model whose requests were blocked loses five of twenty-five scenarios that way, at the stated minor ages, so its response-conditional effect excludes those conditions. It does not bound them in either direction: nothing was returned there, so what the behaviour would have been is unknown. The end-to-end view is where the blocked requests are counted.

label: tab:safety-controls
caption: Planned controls. The trajectory contrast on Refusal Rate run in the three strata whose expected answer does not change with age, percentage points with 95 per cent bootstrap intervals, adjusted within the planned control family of eighteen tests. A control that does not reach significance has not been shown to be null; what the interval excludes is the whole of what these rows establish. No equivalence claim is made, because no smallest effect worth caring about has been justified for this measure.

label: tab:safety-cues
caption: Implicit cue contrasts on Refusal Rate within Age Restricted scenarios, percentage points with 95 per cent bootstrap intervals, paired within scenario. Direction contrasts compare a minor cue against an adult cue inside one cue family and form a secondary family. Channel contrasts compare the two cue families at the same age band, are a planned control of twelve, corrected separately: if the two channels are not interchangeable then a direction effect cannot be attributed to the age band alone.

label: tab:safety-category
caption: Refusal Rate by prompt category on Harmful scenarios. The effect is the mean across the ten harm domains of the within-domain difference, Instruction minus Information, in percentage points, with a 95 per cent interval from a stratified bootstrap that holds the domain composition fixed and a p value from a permutation that shuffles the category label within a domain. The level columns are unadjusted marginal rates and are shown for context only. Age Restricted scenarios are entirely Instruction, so the interaction with stated age is not identified.

label: tab:safety-domains
caption: Refusal Rate on Harmful scenarios by harm domain, per cent of returned responses, ordered by the macro-average. Descriptive only. The design allocates between two and three Age Restricted scenarios to each domain, too few to support an age contrast within a domain, so no inferential family is declared for this cut.

label: tab:safety-characteristics
caption: Every annotated characteristic beyond the outcome, tested one at a time. Prevalence is the share of returned responses on which the characteristic was recorded; a value the classifier returned in a form the schema does not accept is missing rather than absent and is outside its own denominator. The effect compares the six stated minor ages against the two stated adult ages, percentage points with 95 per cent bootstrap intervals, paired within scenario and pooled across strata, adjusted within the response characteristics family of forty-two tests. The group column orders the rows and is not a composite. A characteristic below the calibration agreement floor of Cohen kappa 0.70 is shown with its prevalence and carries no test. Part of any movement follows the shift in the outcome mix rather than a change in how a given outcome is written, which Chapter 5.4 separates.

label: tab:safety-register
caption: The safety test register after Benjamini and Hochberg correction within each declared family. Tests counts every registered row and tested counts those carrying a p value; the macro-average row of each contrast is registered for its interval and is not tested. Families are corrected independently, so an exploratory test cannot cost a primary one its significance and the primary family cannot be widened by adding tests to it. This is research audit infrastructure rather than a results table.

label: tab:safety-trend
caption: Whether Refusal Rate moves monotonically with the stated age. The statistic is the mean over scenarios of the Spearman rank correlation between stated age and refusal rate within that scenario, across the eight stated ages, within Age Restricted. It is not a textbook Spearman test and is not reported as one: flat scenarios enter at zero and the correlations are then averaged over scenarios, which puts the statistic outside the reference distribution a Spearman p value assumes. It is tested instead by permuting the stated age labels within a scenario, which is the exchangeability the null implies, and adjusted within the secondary age trend family of six tests. A negative correlation means refusal falls as the stated age rises. A scenario whose refusal rate never moves has no rank correlation and is read as no trend rather than dropped, which is conservative: dropping it would restrict the statistic to scenarios that had already moved.

label: tab:safety-sensitivity
caption: Leave-one-model-out sensitivity on the three primary contrasts, percentage points. Each of the first six rows gives the macro-average recomputed with that model withheld. The sensitivity check never replaces the reported six model figure. Sign consistency is descriptive of this panel and is not a test; it is reported because a panel result built from six effects that agree in direction supports a different claim from one built from six that do not.

label: tab:safety-borderline
caption: Sensitivity on the borderline characteristic. Eligibility Statement clears the calibration agreement floor at Cohen kappa 0.702, but on an interval running from 0.488 to 0.868 and at a prevalence of 2.3 per cent in the sample, so it is not as securely measured as Service Signpost at 0.991. The second row withholds it and re-corrects the family. The final column counts the tests on the remaining characteristics whose significance changes as a result, which is the only way the borderline characteristic could affect a conclusion that does not rest on it directly.
